tulisokibart.name: Tulisokibart
tulisokibart.headline: First TL1A antibody to reach Phase 3. The class-defining readout — ATLAS-UC topline expected ~Nov 2026 will set the bar for all TL1A programs.
tulisokibart.mechanism_short: Blocks TL1A binding to DR3 receptor, suppressing T cell and innate lymphoid cell (ILC) activation in the gut mucosa. Pathway-selective anti-inflammatory without broad immunosuppression.
tulisokibart.mechanism_detail: Tulisokibart is a fully human IgG1 anti-TL1A monoclonal antibody. TL1A (TNFSF15) is expressed by gut endothelial cells, macrophages, and dendritic cells in response to inflammatory stimuli. It binds Death Receptor 3 (DR3/TNFRSF25) on T cells, particularly CD4+ effector cells and regulatory T cells (Tregs), as well as ILC2 and ILC3 populations. DR3 signaling drives expansion of Th9, Th17, and Th1 subsets — all central to IBD pathophysiology. Notably, TL1A-DR3 co-stimulates T cell activation in concert with IL-23, suggesting why dual blockade (bispecific) may outperform monotherapy.
tulisokibart.companion_dx: TNFSF15 haplotype — ~60% of IBD patients carry risk variants associated with TL1A overexpression. Prometheus co-developed a companion diagnostic to identify likely responders. Merck has continued this strategy, potentially enabling a label restricted to biomarker-positive patients (higher responder rate, stronger efficacy numbers, payer differentiation).

clinical_summary.result: 26.5% clinical remission vs 1.5% placebo at Wk12 (composite estimand). Favorable safety profile. Supported Ph3 advancement.
Topline expected ~Nov 2026. Primary: clinical remission at Wk12/52. Co-primary in both induction and maintenance.
CD extension. Primary completion Oct 2028. If ATLAS-UC succeeds, converts UC-only asset into full IBD franchise.

tulisokibart.deal_context: Merck acquired Prometheus Biosciences for ~$10.8B in 2023, primarily for tulisokibart and the companion Dx program. This was the largest IBD-focused acquisition since AbbVie/Allergan. The price reflects Merck's view that TL1A represents a multi-billion-dollar IBD franchise opportunity, particularly with companion Dx enabling payer differentiation.
tulisokibart.bd_lens: First mover advantage in Ph3. Companion Dx creates precision medicine positioning — Merck can potentially show >40% remission rates in biomarker+ patients vs. ~27% all-comers. However, single-agent TL1A may be the bar that bispecific TL1A×IL-23 programs must clear. The Nov 2026 readout will determine whether this is a platform or a one-drug story.
key_questions: Does ATLAS-UC hit the primary composite remission endpoint?
Does the TNFSF15 biomarker enable a precision label with higher remission rates?
If positive, does this validate TL1A as a platform target or commoditize the mechanism?
How does Merck position tulisokibart vs. dupilumab and risankizumab in UC treatment algorithm?

duvakitug.name: Duvakitug
duvakitug.headline: Strongest Ph2 efficacy signal in the TL1A class — 48% UC remission at Ph2. Backed by Sanofi's global commercial infrastructure. Considered the most commercially formidable asset in the TL1A space.
duvakitug.mechanism_short: Anti-TL1A monoclonal antibody. Same target as tulisokibart, different antibody with distinct binding characteristics and potentially different epitope.
duvakitug.mechanism_detail: Duvakitug was originally developed by Teva and co-developed with Sanofi. It targets the same TL1A-DR3 axis as other anti-TL1A antibodies. The superior Ph2 efficacy (48% vs. 26.5% for tulisokibart) likely reflects a combination of: potentially superior potency, different patient population selection, or different estimand/endpoint design. The 900mg dose in RELIEVE-UC showed the highest signal. Sanofi brings global commercial infrastructure and IBD expertise from the Dupixent franchise (though Dupixent was not approved for IBD).

clinical_summary.result: 48% clinical remission at 900mg Wk14 vs 20% placebo (composite estimand). CD arm: 48% endoscopic response. Strongest Ph2 signal in TL1A class.

duvakitug.deal_context: Teva partnered with Sanofi for duvakitug, giving Sanofi global development and commercial rights. Sanofi paid significant upfront for this, viewing TL1A as a key pillar of its immunology pipeline following the success of Dupixent. The combination of Teva's IBD development expertise and Sanofi's scale makes this the most commercially threatening TL1A asset.
duvakitug.bd_lens: 48% Ph2 remission is exceptional but requires Ph3 confirmation. If ATLAS-UC (tulisokibart) reads positive first (Nov 2026) and achieves strong remission, it sets the clinical bar. Duvakitug needs to show comparable or superior efficacy in Ph3 to justify premium positioning. Sanofi's commercial reach means even a 'second to market' outcome could dominate commercially.
key_questions: Will the 48% Ph2 remission translate to Ph3?
Does duvakitug differentiate from tulisokibart on efficacy or label?
Can Sanofi accelerate enrollment to narrow the readout gap with Merck?
Will regulators require head-to-head data vs. tulisokibart if both are approved?

afimkibart.name: Afimkibart
afimkibart.headline: Highest-risk Ph3 program in the TL1A class. Ph2b primary endpoint was missed, yet Roche committed to Ph3 based on secondary endpoints and open-label extension data. The most controversial advancement in the field.
afimkibart.mechanism_short: Anti-TL1A antibody. Same target as tulisokibart and duvakitug, developed by Pfizer before divestiture to Roivant/Telavant and acquisition by Roche.
afimkibart.mechanism_detail: Originally developed by Pfizer, then licensed to Roivant Sciences (via Telavant, Roivant's IBD subsidiary). Roche acquired Telavant for ~$7.1B in December 2023, before the TUSCANY-2 Ph2b full results were available. When TUSCANY-2 data readout in 2024 showed a missed primary endpoint (24% vs 12% remission at Wk14, p=NS), Roche's $7.1B investment came under scrutiny. Roche justified Ph3 advancement based on: positive secondary endpoints, 43% remission in OLE for biomarker+ patients, and regulatory precedent for secondary endpoint reliance.

clinical_summary.result: PRIMARY MISSED: 24% UC remission vs 12% placebo at Wk14, not statistically significant. Secondary endpoints positive. 43% remission in biomarker+ OLE patients.

afimkibart.deal_context: Roche paid ~$7.1B for Telavant, making afimkibart the most expensive TL1A acquisition. The deal predated the TUSCANY-2 Ph2b miss, which reduced confidence in the program. Roche committed to Ph3 regardless, betting on: biomarker+ subgroup data, regulatory flexibility, and the strategic importance of having an IBD biologic in their portfolio.
afimkibart.bd_lens: The highest-stakes binary event in the TL1A class. If AMETRINE Ph3 succeeds despite Ph2b miss, it validates Roche's thesis and rewards the $7.1B bet. If Ph3 fails, it will be a major write-down and a cautionary tale about proceeding to Ph3 without Ph2b success. Partners and biomarker companies watching closely for TNFSF15 biomarker enrichment data.
key_questions: Can Ph3 succeed despite Ph2b primary endpoint miss?
Will the TNFSF15 biomarker enable a responder-enriched Ph3 to succeed?
Is Roche's Ph3 design optimized based on TUSCANY-2 learnings?
What happens to the $7.1B investment if Ph3 fails?

mt251.name: MT-251
mt251.headline: First-in-class FcRn-recycling TL1A×IL-23p19 bispecific. Extended half-life design from the ground up. Ph1 SAD/MAD data expected Q1 2027 — will be the first human PK/safety data for any TL1A×IL-23p19 bispecific.
mt251.mechanism_short: Simultaneously blocks TL1A and IL-23p19 in a single molecule. FcRn-recycling extends half-life beyond standard IgG, enabling potentially monthly or less frequent dosing.
mt251.mechanism_detail: MT-251 is Mirador's lead bispecific antibody targeting both TL1A (upstream T cell activator) and IL-23p19 (Th17/ILC3 driver) simultaneously. The FcRn (neonatal Fc receptor) recycling mechanism involves engineering the antibody's Fc region to bind FcRn with higher affinity at endosomal pH, extending the antibody's recycling loop and dramatically increasing serum half-life beyond the ~21-day standard IgG baseline. Extended t½ means less frequent dosing — a key commercial differentiator in IBD where treatment compliance and infusion burden affect both patients and payers. The dual blockade rationale: TL1A and IL-23 co-activate the same T cell subsets synergistically; blocking both simultaneously prevents the escape through either pathway.
mt251.companion_dx: Mirador has not publicly disclosed a companion diagnostic strategy. The FcRn platform approach suggests they may be betting on broad patient access rather than biomarker-restricted label.

clinical_summary.result: Ongoing. Q1 2027 readout (10+ events). Will establish safety, PK, half-life, and dose escalation in healthy volunteers.

mt251.deal_context: Mirador is an independent company backed by significant venture funding. They have not announced a partnership, which either means they are building toward a pivotal program independently or are waiting for Ph1 data before partnering. Independent status allows them to retain full value but requires substantial capital for Ph2/Ph3.
mt251.bd_lens: The most scientifically interesting bispecific in the TL1A class from a mechanism standpoint. The FcRn platform is a genuine differentiator — if Ph1 confirms extended half-life (>4-6 weeks), it creates a compelling 'best in format' argument. Q1 2027 readout will be the first bispecific TL1A Ph1 data and will generate significant BD interest.
key_questions: What half-life does MT-251 achieve in humans? >4 weeks = major differentiator
Is the safety profile consistent with monotherapy anti-TL1A and anti-IL-23 agents?
Will Mirador partner before or after Ph2?
Does FcRn recycling work as well in IBD patients (GI protein loss) as in healthy volunteers?

tezepelumab.name: Tezepelumab
tezepelumab.headline: The benchmark for all TSLP-targeting programs. 70% AAER reduction across ALL asthma endotypes including low-eosinophil patients. The first biologic to work regardless of inflammatory subtype.
tezepelumab.mechanism_short: Blocks TSLP from binding its receptor (TSLPRα), preventing the initiation of the type 2 inflammatory cascade at the epithelial barrier. Upstream suppression covers both eosinophilic and non-eosinophilic inflammation.
tezepelumab.mechanism_detail: TSLP is an epithelial cytokine released in response to physical or chemical damage to airway epithelium — triggered by allergens, viruses, cigarette smoke, and air pollutants. It acts on dendritic cells (DCs), mast cells, basophils, and ILC2s to drive both Type 2 (IL-4, IL-5, IL-13) and non-Type 2 (IL-17, IL-25) inflammation. Unlike IL-4/13 inhibitors (dupilumab) or IL-5 inhibitors (mepolizumab), TSLP sits upstream of the branch point — it activates cells that then produce both eosinophilic and neutrophilic mediators. This explains why tezepelumab works across all endotypes: it prevents the upstream signal that initiates all downstream inflammatory programs. Tezepelumab binds TSLP at its receptor interaction site, blocking engagement with TSLPRα/IL-7Rα heterodimer on immune cells.

clinical_summary.result: 70% AAER reduction vs placebo (treatment policy estimand). Positive in ALL subgroups including eos<150. This is the benchmark. Approved 2021.
Did not meet primary endpoint on OCS reduction but showed positive AAER secondary. Label does not require specific eos threshold.
Ongoing. Topline expected 2026-2027. If positive, expands addressable market significantly.

tezepelumab.deal_context: Amgen originally developed tezepelumab and co-developed with AstraZeneca. AstraZeneca holds primary commercial rights. The NAVIGATOR result (treatment policy estimand — counting exacerbations even when patients changed medication mid-trial) was critical: it made the bar for any competing TSLP asset tougher, since reviewers will compare using the same estimand.
tezepelumab.bd_lens: Tezepelumab is the benchmark, not a BD target. Its importance is as the bar every new TSLP program must clear — and the evidence base that TSLP blockade is a validated mechanism. For bispecifics adding IL-33 blockade on top, the question is: can you beat 70% AAER? The treatment policy estimand is the key: all new programs should use this to enable head-to-head comparison.
key_questions: Will SUNRISE COPD Ph3 succeed? If yes, opens a >$10B additional market.
How should bispecific programs design trials relative to tezepelumab efficacy?
Does tezepelumab face generics/biosimilars threat from emerging long-acting anti-TSLPs?
Can extended-half-life anti-TSLPs (bosakitug, HBM9378) match NAVIGATOR outcomes with less frequent dosing?

qx031n.name: QX031N
qx031n.company: Qyuns Therapeutics (CN) → licensed to Roche (Oct 2025, $75M upfront / $1.07B total)
qx031n.headline: The most strategically important single bispecific asset in the respiratory space. $1.07B deal with Roche — the largest TSLP bispecific deal to date. Roche combines QX031N with astegolimab (anti-ST2/IL-33R, Ph3) to own the full IL-33 pathway.
qx031n.mechanism_short: Blocks both TSLP and IL-33 simultaneously — the two primary epithelial alarmins in respiratory inflammation. Designed to provide more complete upstream suppression than tezepelumab (anti-TSLP alone) by eliminating IL-33's independent activation of ILC2s and mast cells.
qx031n.mechanism_detail: TSLP and IL-33 are released simultaneously from damaged airway epithelium — they are co-produced in response to the same triggers (allergens, viruses, smoke). While tezepelumab blocks TSLP, IL-33 continues to activate ILC2s, mast cells, and eosinophils via ST2 independently. QX031N's dual blockade prevents both arms of the alarmin response. In COPD specifically, IL-33 independently drives AECOPD in certain patient subgroups, and anti-IL-33 (itepekimab) already has proven efficacy in COPD (AERIFY-1/-2). Therefore, TSLP+IL-33 co-blockade combines the breadth of tezepelumab (all asthma endotypes) with the IL-33 axis validated by itepekimab in COPD.

clinical_summary.result: Enrolling. ~2027 first-in-human data. Safety, PK, dose escalation in healthy volunteers.

qx031n.deal_context: Roche paid $75M upfront for a preclinical asset — the largest upfront for any TSLP bispecific. Context: Roche already holds astegolimab (anti-ST2, anti-IL-33R) in Ph3 PACIFIC (asthma) and OBERON/MIRANDA (COPD). QX031N gives Roche both upstream TSLP blockade AND IL-33 blockade in a single molecule, complementing astegolimab's IL-33R approach. This positions Roche as the dominant player in the alarmin pathway across respiratory disease. Qyuns has now completed 3 major out-licensing deals in the bispecific space, establishing itself as the most prolific Chinese bispecific out-licensor.
qx031n.bd_lens: The $1.07B valuation at preclinical stage reflects: (1) Roche's strategic interest in owning the alarmin pathway, (2) Validated biology from tezepelumab + itepekimab, (3) Long-acting format enabling Q8W+ dosing, (4) COPD + Asthma combined market. Competing companies developing TSLP×IL-33 bispecifics (Odyssey Therapeutics, Sinomab) should note this as their valuation benchmark.
key_questions: Will Ph1 PK confirm the extended half-life enabling Q8W or Q12W dosing?
How does Roche integrate QX031N with astegolimab — replace, complement, or compete?
Will bispecific TSLP×IL-33 blockade show additive efficacy over tezepelumab in clinical trials?
What patient population (COPD, severe asthma, or all-comers) will Roche prioritize first?

bosakitug.name: Bosakitug
bosakitug.company: Biosion (CN) → Aclaris Therapeutics (licensed Nov 2024, $40M upfront / >$900M total)
bosakitug.headline: Long-acting anti-TSLP monoAb — first proxy for whether extended half-life (vs. tezepelumab's standard Q4W) provides comparable or superior efficacy with less frequent dosing. Ph2 asthma data H2 2026.
bosakitug.mechanism_short: Same TSLP target as tezepelumab but engineered for extended serum half-life via Fc region modifications. Less frequent dosing (Q8W, Q12W) if efficacy is maintained — a key commercial differentiator for asthma where compliance with monthly injections is challenging.
bosakitug.mechanism_detail: Bosakitug is a next-generation anti-TSLP antibody designed with half-life extension technology. The standard tezepelumab requires 210mg Q4W (monthly) subcutaneous injection. A long-acting version with t½ >6-8 weeks would enable Q8W (bimonthly) or Q12W (quarterly) dosing — substantially reducing treatment burden for patients with chronic asthma and improving compliance and persistence. Aclaris paid $40M upfront for this asset, primarily for the US market. Biosion retains an additional TSLP-based asset (BSI-502, a TSLP×IL-4Rα bispecific, Ph1) creating a dual franchise.

clinical_summary.result: H2 2026 data readout. Primary endpoint: AAER reduction. First clinical comparison point for long-acting vs. standard anti-TSLP dosing.

bosakitug.deal_context: $40M upfront for Ph1→Ph2 stage long-acting anti-TSLP. Sets the lower bound of TSLP deal valuation for early-stage/long-acting mono programs. Aclaris is a US dermatology/immunology company expanding into respiratory — the TSLP asset in AD (atopic dermatitis) is also relevant given TSLP's role in skin barrier inflammation.
bosakitug.bd_lens: H2 2026 data will be the first real-world proxy for long-acting TSLP performance. Key read: if bosakitug shows AAER reduction comparable to tezepelumab at Q8W dosing, it validates the long-acting format as a commercial differentiator. This has direct implications for HBM9378/SKB378 (Harbour+Kelun) and Xencor's XmAb942 (t½ >71 days).
key_questions: What half-life does bosakitug achieve — Q8W or Q12W dosing?
Is AAER reduction comparable to tezepelumab's 70% benchmark?
Does Aclaris have the commercial muscle to compete with AZ/Amgen in respiratory?
Will AD data support a dual asthma + AD label (larger commercial opportunity)?

itepekimab.name: Itepekimab
itepekimab.headline: First anti-IL-33 biologic approved in COPD (Apr 2025). Validates the IL-33 pathway independently in COPD and motivates TSLP×IL-33 bispecific development. Narrower label than tezepelumab — ex-smokers only, eosinophil threshold required.
itepekimab.mechanism_short: Neutralizes free IL-33 before it can bind ST2 receptor, preventing ILC2/mast cell/eosinophil activation in the airway. Type 2 and structural remodeling suppression.
itepekimab.mechanism_detail: IL-33 is a nuclear alarmin released from airway epithelial cells, smooth muscle cells, and fibroblasts in response to cell damage (necrosis, mechanical stress, viral infection). It binds ST2 (IL-1RL1) on ILC2s, mast cells, basophils, eosinophils, and regulatory T cells. IL-33 is a key driver of eosinophilic inflammation and — in COPD specifically — promotes AECOPD events independent of TSLP. Itepekimab directly neutralizes IL-33, preventing ST2 engagement. Unlike tozorakimab (anti-ST2/IL-33R), itepekimab captures free circulating IL-33 rather than blocking the receptor. Sanofi/Regeneron's AERIFY-1/-2 Ph3 trials showed ~25% AECOPD reduction vs placebo in ex-smokers with eos ≥150 cells/μL — clinically meaningful but narrower population than tezepelumab.

clinical_summary.result: POSITIVE: ~25% AECOPD reduction vs placebo in ex-smokers (eos ≥150 cells/μL). Approved in COPD 2025.
Ongoing in severe uncontrolled asthma. Results pending.

itepekimab.deal_context: Part of Sanofi/Regeneron's broader IL-33 pathway strategy alongside dupilumab (anti-IL-4Rα). Sanofi now has three approved or late-stage biologics covering TSLP (via QX031N in pipeline), IL-33 (itepekimab), and IL-4/13 (dupilumab) — an unmatched alarmin pathway portfolio.
itepekimab.bd_lens: Itepekimab's approval in COPD is a landmark for alarmin-targeting — it proves the pathway has regulatory precedent beyond asthma. The narrow label (ex-smokers, eos threshold) creates an opening for broader-acting agents like QX031N (TSLP×IL-33). The 25% AECOPD reduction sets the floor; TSLP×IL-33 bispecifics will need to show significantly higher reduction to justify new development.
key_questions: Does itepekimab expand to additional COPD subgroups (current smokers, low-eos)?
How does tozorakimab (anti-ST2) compare to itepekimab in direct comparison?
Does itepekimab achieve asthma approval — and if so, how does its eos-restricted label compare to tezepelumab?
Can TSLP×IL-33 bispecifics demonstrate additive efficacy over each agent alone?
